Customer to provide final 200 labeled prompts for regression analysis by 2025-03-06
SRE/SE to schedule on-prem networking checklist call re: VPC peering by 2025-03-10
Send security docs (SOC2 + encryption/KMS note) to Priya by 2025-03-05
action_items: Sofia Patel - Share updated prompt set and scoring spreadsheet - 2025-03-06
Diego Ramirez - Run batch of 5k evals with caching on/off and send CSV - 2025-03-11
Lena Cho - Label edge-case 200 prompts and return to Redwood - 2025-03-06
Priya Nair - Confirm data retention & KMS requirements, send checklist - 2025-03-07
header: Date: 2025-03-04T14:00Z | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (NimbusHealth ML), Mark Rivera (Nimbus Product), Priya Nair (Nimbus Security), Jamal Ortiz (Nimbus Data) | Recording: enabled
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review quality eval results from week 3. Customer presented regression signals on clinical summarization prompts after switching to quantized X-3B model. Redwood SE proposed tuning suggestions (prompt engineering, reranker thresholding, KV/prefix caching tweaks) and a 5k benchmark to isolate cause. Security and next steps discussed: share prompt set, run evals with/without caching, provide SOC2 and KMS notes, schedule VPC peering checklist.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, this is the week 3 POC sync to focus on quality evals. we got the report from Lena so we'll jump in. Uh Diego and I will kick it off, then we'll pass to Lena for the result walk-through.
[00:18] Diego Ramirez: quick note, recording is on. I'll share my screen after Lena goes through the slides.
[00:30] Mark Rivera: cool thanks Sofia.
[00:33] Lena Cho: ok so hi all, I'm lena. we ran the labeled prompt set from week 1 and week 2 and compared against the new X-3B quantized run. overall pass rate dipped ~6% but more importantly clinical hallucination cases went up on a subset. I'll share the spreadsheet link in chat.
[00:55] Priya Nair: can you define hallucination here? is it confident but wrong facts about patient histories?
[01:02] Lena Cho: yeah exactly, confident statements like "patient has no allergies" when input had allergy note. also truncation on long SOAP notes.
[01:15] Diego Ramirez: hmm ok, do you have the prompt variant that produced the regression? was it the new condensed system prompt?
[01:24] Lena Cho: we switched to the shorter instruction to reduce token usage per call — we thought quantization + smaller prompt would cut cost. the prompt set is in the shared drive.
[01:36] Sofia Patel: quick clarifying Q: when you say quantized X-3B, is that the 4-bit int8 style or our 16-bit mixed?
[01:45] Lena Cho: it's our internal 4-bit quant on the host config. Diego, you ran an A/B with non-quantized?
[01:53] Diego Ramirez: yes we re-ran 300 samples on float32 host and 3k on quantized. the float run looked closer to baseline. quantized + short prompt combo showed the worst degradation.
[02:10] Jamal Ortiz: we also saw more prefix KV miss patterns, sometimes the K V cache didn't warm up properly — maybe the batch/pinning config.
[02:20] Diego Ramirez: that's important — caching behavior can change generation consistency, especially with small context and quantization noise. we'll check the continuous batching and kv cache settings, there might be a mismatch from the default.
[02:36] Mark Rivera: what's the measured latency delta? cost delta?
[02:40] Diego Ramirez: quantized run saved ~32% per-token cost but latency was slightly lower but within our SLO. The tradeoff is small model artifacts.
[02:50] Priya Nair: security Q: if we change to dedicated or private, what's data retention and KMS chain? we need to know before we escalate.
[02:58] Sofia Patel: we can share SOC2 report and KMS integration notes, Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. we'll attach docs.
[03:08] Lena Cho: ok i'll walk through a few examples — screen share now.
[03:16] [screen share noise]
[03:30] Lena Cho: example 1: prompt id 1122, baseline summarized the med hx correctly. quantized short prompt omitted allergy line and added an incorrect med. example 2: long SOAP note truncated mid-sentence. here are the reduced-confidence tokens in the log.
[03:50] Diego Ramirez: are you using our reranker at the top-k step or just thresholding the final token probs?
[03:58] Lena Cho: currently post-filtering simple heuristics, not full reranker.
[04:04] Diego Ramirez: ok suggest enabling a lightweight reranker for the prompt set that prioritizes factual mentions (allergy, meds) and using a fallback to float run for flagged cases. we can do hybrid routing: cheap quantized by default, route flagged prompts to float model.
[04:22] Mark Rivera: hybrid sounds good but cost could jump. do you have estimated unit economics?
[04:27] Sofia Patel: yes Diego will run an analysis — cost per 1k with 10% fallback to float vs full float; we'll include token-level breakdown.
[04:36] Priya Nair: also need RBAC around who can trigger fallback — we don't want product to accidentally route all traffic to float.
[04:44] Diego Ramirez: Redwood Console supports per-route policies and role-based rollout controls. we can lock the fallback policy behind admin role.
[04:52] Lena Cho: one more note about prompts: some of our prompt templates remove patient identifiers which changes context shape — that may be amplifying quantization errors on long-tail cases.
[05:03] Sofia Patel: good call. action: please send the exact prompt templates so Diego can reproduce. Lena: is that in the google drive?
[05:11] Lena Cho: yes, link in chat.
[05:14] [chat ping sound]
[05:20] Diego Ramirez: ok next, can we run a 5k benchmark that toggles caching and reranker? my plan: run 5k w/ caching on + reranker, 5k caching off + reranker, 5k caching on no reranker, compare metrics — accuracy, hallucination count, truncation rate, latency.
[05:39] Jamal Ortiz: timeline?
[05:41] Diego Ramirez: i can run it by next week given GPU availability — target 2025-03-11.
[05:47] Lena Cho: please also include the exact random seed and sampling params, we saw sampling temp changes also cause variance.
[05:54] Diego Ramirez: will do, i'll include sampling, top-k, top-p and seed.
[05:59] Mark Rivera: regarding guardrails, can we get a pre-output safety filter to catch hallucinated facts?
[06:06] Diego Ramirez: yes we have a post-processing safety step and token-level score threshold. it can be tuned for clinical entities. we can also add entity-checking against the input.
[06:16] Priya Nair: and audit logs for every fallback event? we need a traceable record to meet compliance.
[06:22] Sofia Patel: audit logs are part of Dedicated and Private modes, we'll show sample traces.
[06:28] Lena Cho: one more regression detail: some errors triggered specifically on lab-result extraction prompts. likely tokenization edge-case on certain unicode chars.
[06:39] Diego Ramirez: good to capture. please add 50 lab-extraction edge cases to the labeled file.
[06:45] Lena Cho: will do.
[06:47] [pause, typing]
[06:55] Sofia Patel: ok let's talk about success criteria for next sync — do we want to see <2% regression on labeled set and hallucination reduced to baseline?
[07:06] Lena Cho: yes that seems fair. also show cost delta if we enable hybrid fallback.
[07:13] Mark Rivera: plus a security sign-off note from Priya.
[07:17] Priya Nair: i'll need the sample audit logs and KMS flowchart to sign off.
[07:23] Diego Ramirez: noted.
[07:26] [09:00] Diego Ramirez: switching gears, quick note about deployment: if you prefer Dedicated we can pre-configure VPC peering. that would eliminate egress concerns and allows customer-managed KMS.
[09:14] Jamal Ortiz: timeline for Dedicated?
[09:17] Sofia Patel: Depends on contract, but we can spin reserved capacity in 2-4 weeks once PO is processed. For POC it's often easier to keep hosted but simulate VPC via private endpoints.
[09:31] Priya Nair: is there any difference in logging retention between hosted and dedicated?
[09:36] Diego Ramirez: dedicated gives customizable retention windows and you can push logs to your SIEM. hosted has standard retention but we can purchase extended retention.
[09:48] Lena Cho: back to quality—diego can you outline the specific config you'll toggle for the benchmark?
[09:54] Diego Ramirez: yes: 1) quantized X-3B w/ caching on/off. 2) quantized w/ reranker on/off. 3) float32 baseline. 4) hybrid routing with 10% fallback parameter. I'll output accuracy, hallucination count, truncation events, latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k.
[10:13] Mark Rivera: good. make sure to annotate examples where model "hallucinates" with input snippet and model output.
[10:20] Diego Ramirez: yep we'll include model logs and token probs where possible.
[10:24] Sofia Patel: ok any other risks, blockers from customer side?
[10:29] Lena Cho: just labeling capacity and time. we'll prioritize the 200 high-risk prompts first.
[10:34] Jamal Ortiz: data access for Redwood to run evals — we'll provide a temporary s3 bucket and role.
[10:39] Diego Ramirez: perfect, please send role and bucket path.
[10:43] [15:00] Sofia Patel: closing recap: Diego will run 5k benchmark and share CSV + cost analysis by 3/11; Sofia will share SOC2 + KMS notes by 3/5; Lena will send labeled 200 prompts and 50 lab-edge cases by 3/6; Priya will review audit logs. We'll reconvene next Tuesday for results.
[15:28] Mark Rivera: thanks all.
[15:30] Priya Nair: thanks.
[15:32] Lena Cho: thanks.
[15:35] Diego Ramirez: thanks everyone, i'll post the run plan in the shared doc.
[15:40] Sofia Patel: meeting adjourned.
[15:42] [recording stop]
